lines.text: You row toward a lighthouse that should be lit. It has been dark for eleven days.
lines.beat_before: hook: from the relief boat, the dark tower on the island

lines.text: December, nineteen hundred. A steamer passing the Flannan Isles sees that the lamp is out.
lines.beat_before: night: a steamer passes; the tower is dark

lines.text: Storms keep the relief boat away until the day after Christmas.
No flag. No one comes down to meet it.
lines.beat_before: the east landing: the empty flagstaff, no one on the steps
the walk up; the door; inside

lines.text: One set of oilskins still hangs on its hook.
Three keepers lived here. All three are gone.
On the west landing, iron railings are torn and bent, high above the sea.
lines.beat_before: stinger in silence; the west landing

lines.text: The official report suggested two men went down to secure the landing in the storm, and the third ran out without his coat.
lines.beat_before: the storm: lanterns going down; a man at the door

lines.text: A huge wave took them. They were never found.
But no one knows what he saw from the doorway, that made him run.
